newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia needs to simplify, look abroad - AFMA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia needs to simplify, look abroad - AFMA.

text.p: Australia needs to simplify both its taxation and regulative systems, and be more outward looking if its financial centre is to compete with other financial markets in the Asian region, according to one industry body.

Releasing its 1996 Australian Financial Market Report, Australian Financial Markets Association's (AFMA) chief executive, Ken Farrow said local financial markets will be forced to look further afield in coming years.
AFMA's report showed Australia's wholsale financial markets recorded a net turnover of around A$27 trillion in the year to June 30, down A$1.0 trillion from 1994/95.
This also compares with A$25 trillion in 1993/94 and the A$21.0 trillion in 1992/93.

"The plateau of the past two years is broadly explained by changing markets and economic conditions," Farrow said. "It also suggests the Australian markets are in a stage of transition and in need of infrastructure rationalisation."
However, equities had reported remarkably strong growth in 1996/96, culminating in a 35 percent increase in turnover.
Farrow saw this growth as reflection of the Australian Stock Exchange's (ASX) determined drive to attract offshore business combined with the reduction in transaction costs.

The reduction in the country's stamp duties had provided an incentive for the equities markets, but other taxes needed to be looked at, and impediments to Australia's international competitiveness still needed to be addressed, Farrow said.

"(Taxation) needs to be rationalised and simplified, and not necessarily reduced," he said. Local financial markets also need to promote themselves more to compete with growing centres offshore, such as Singapore.
Thirdly "We have to make sure the outcome of the Wallis inquiry is a simplifaction of the regulatory process," he added.

A recent survey conducted by the Securities Industry Research Centre of Asia-Pacific (SIRCA) showed that Australia's foreign exchange and stock markets had lost ground against other major centres in the Asia region and only interest rate derivatives exhibited a competitive position.
The SIRCA survey was commissioned by AFMA.
